title: 2.5 Trillion South Korean Won Invested in AI Infrastructure, the National AI Computing Center of South Korea Breaks Ground with a Target of 2028
excerpt: According to South Korean media EtNews, the Korea AI Computing Center (KOACC) was officially broken ground on August 3 in the Solar City data center park in Sun
content_html:
According to South Korean media EtNews, the Korea AI Computing Center (KOACC) was officially broken ground on August 3 in the Solar City data center park in Sunan County, Jeollanam-do. The total investment reaches 2.5 trillion KRW (approximately 11.838 billion RMB), with the goal of completion and operation by 2028. This is one of the largest national-level investment projects in AI infrastructure in South Korea so far.

The equity structure of the project reflects a strategic intention of deep government-business integration. Samsung SDS holds 30% and becomes the largest shareholder, while government agencies such as the Ministry of Science and Technology, Financial Supervisory Service, and National Growth Fund collectively hold 29%. NAVER Cloud follows closely with 26.1%. Companies such as Kakao, KT Group, Samsung Electronics, and Samsung C&T also participated in the investment, forming the KOACC alliance, which is responsible for the comprehensive construction and operation of the data center.

Targeting the Global Market, Competing for Computing Power Authority with High Cost-Effectiveness

After its completion, the data center will provide high-level, cost-effective AI computing facilities to the global market, aiming to secure a place for South Korea in the global AI computing power competition. Currently, the KOACC alliance has submitted an electricity application to the Korea Electric Power Corporation and is simultaneously advancing the construction of supporting infrastructure such as water supply pipelines.

In addition to commercial computing power rental services, the South Korean government has also planned a dedicated research area in the center, providing a verification environment for domestically developed NPU (Neural Processing Unit), promoting the acceleration of breakthroughs in the AI custom chip sector of the South Korean semiconductor industry. This layout means that the center is not only a computing power supply node but also a key test field for South Korea's strategy of semiconductor self-reliance.

From Samsung leading the initiative to government investment, from power infrastructure to chip development, this computing center carries not only 2.5 trillion KRW in infrastructure investment, but also South Korea's core bet on securing computing power autonomy in the global AI landscape. As AI computing infrastructure becomes the new focus of competition among major powers, South Korea's move is undoubtedly resolute.

content_html_zh:
据韩国媒体 EtNews 报道，韩国人工智能计算中心（KOACC）于 8 月 3 日在全罗南道顺安郡 Solar City 数据中心园区正式破土动工。 总投资达2.5万亿韩元（约118.38亿元人民币），目标2028年建成运营。 这是韩国迄今为止最大的国家级人工智能基础设施投资项目之一。

该项目的股权结构体现了政商深度融合的战略意图。 三星SDS持股30%，成为第一大股东，科学技术部、金融监督院、国家成长基金等政府机构合计持股29%。 NAVER Cloud 紧随其后，占 26.1%。 Kakao、KT集团、三星电子、三星物产等公司也参与投资，组成KOACC联盟，负责数据中心的全面建设和运营。

瞄准全球市场，高性价比争夺算力权威

该数据中心建成后，将为全球市场提供高水平、高性价比的AI计算设施，旨在为韩国在全球AI算力竞争中占据一席之地。 目前，KOACC联盟已向韩国电力公司提交电力申请，并同步推进供水管道等配套基础设施建设。

除了商用算力租赁服务外，韩国政府还在该中心规划了专门的研究区域，为国产NPU（神经处理单元）提供验证环境，推动韩国半导体行业AI定制芯片领域加速突破。 这一布局意味着该中心不仅是算力供应节点，也是韩国半导体自力更生战略的关键试验场。

从三星主导倡议到政府投资，从电力基础设施到芯片开发，这个计算中心不仅承载着2.5万亿韩元的基础设施投资，也是韩国在全球AI格局中确保算力自主权的核心赌注。 在AI计算基础设施成为大国竞争新焦点之际，韩国此举无疑是坚决的。
